facts.text: Harriman was founded in 1889 by Frederick Gates along the Emory River and the Cincinnati‑Southern Railroad line.
The town earned the nickname “the town that temperance built” because a group of temperance advocates founded it in the late 19th century.
By 1892, rolling mills, factories, and other businesses had relocated to Harriman, turning it into a bustling industrial center.
A 1890 land sale of 10,000 acres funded the construction of factories, churches, schools, and a hilltop residential neighborhood overlooking the town.
The Emory River forms an oxbow bend that surrounds Harriman’s original section, creating a distinctive waterway around the town.
